newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 15.20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 15.20 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 166 basis points to 15.20 in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 40 billion bolivars of 180- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 16.86 percent coupon for a price of 100.77 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 16.86 percent.

The bank also sold 10 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 17.20 percent coupon at a price of 100.35 percent, and 10 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 17.56 percent coupon at an average price of 99.74 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 284 basis points to 16.67 percent for the 269-day bills, and 232 basis points to 17.87 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
